# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-3 (Extended v61)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; **Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18, 1815; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting and conditions**); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse)**; **1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages)**; **autumn of the first year / 1815 onward (trial aftermath reflected; current narrative time at Dunstead harbor town)**; 1823 October (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs; employed later at Brest as school-ship, part of Mediterranean squadron); **1823 Spanish campaign (war of conquest, corruption alleged, Bourbons misinterpreted as success, led to 1830 revolution)**; 1827 February (M. de Villèle parliamentary remarks on tax collection); 1849 (chapel walls freshly whitewashed); 1861/1862 (narrative reflection, traveller departing from Nivelles toward La Hulpe)
- Primary locations: M. sur M.; Montfermeil; Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; **Hougomont (château, farm, chapel, well, orchard, garden, wood, northern and southern doors, paddock, spiral staircase, chapel with wooden crucifix and Saint Anne statue); Mont-Saint-Jean plateau; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; village of Ohain; hollow road of Ohain (from Braine-l'Alleud); Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Dunstead (harbor town); Montfermeil forest; forge; clearings and thickets; Toulon port; Brest; Mediterranean; Trocadéro; Spain**; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby, Ostcombe, Ravenmere); Kelmere (river crossing); meadow near Genappe; willow at Wilwick; Vincennes; Schoenbrunn; Philippi; Longwood; Saint Helena; Vienna; Pas de Calais; Abbey of Saint-Georges de Bocherville (near Rouen); Rouen; **Balearic Isles; Arsenal quay; Toulon port dry dock; Dungate**

## Montfermeil/Dunstead Community: Ongoing Daily Life and Mysteries

**Boulatruelle's Forest Activity (Late 1823 onward, ongoing)**:
[As previously recorded: mysterious searching with pickaxe; public perception; Thénardier and schoolmaster interrogations; drinking test; suspected robber band affiliation]

**Dunstead Community Daily Actions and Relationships (Autumn period, contemporary narrative)**:
- **Pewyn**: counted coins twice, came up penny short; laughed at story nobody else found funny; **gave Nylia Corrford solemn promise to rebuild the fallen wall at Quenford** (COMMITMENT)
- **Yewyn Corrford**: appeared tired; bought ribbon at stall and regretted it; agreed with Kassa about salt price scandal
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; **gave Lura Haskick solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Stenson family** (COMMITMENT); counted coins twice, came up penny short
- **Nylia Corrford**: complained of aching back; **gave Pewyn Stenenridge solemn promise to rebuild the fallen wall at Quenford** (COMMITMENT)
- **Yera Haskick**: **gave Yewyn Corrford solemn promise to carry a sealed letter to Dungate** (COMMITMENT)
- **Lura Haskick**: recipient of Ulrald's debt-payment promise; mended torn sleeve by window, said little
- **Kassa Brackick**: told Yewyn "The price of salt is a scandal"
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return to Dunstead; **CLAIM**: Luena followed him to Staveford within the month
- **Elra**: spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; walked long way round to avoid muddy square
- **Fenelle**: read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints
- **Other figures**: Marald Corrford asked about rain; Stenson family owed debt by Ulrald
- **Environmental backdrop**: Ruts and puddles after thaw; crooked sun chalked on forge wall; smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; frost silvered hedges overnight; bell for vespers rang thinly; children chased hoop shrieking; cart with turnips creaked past well; dog barked at nothing; wind off water smelled of salt and tar; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps

## The Orion Incident: Rescue at Toulon (October 1823)

**Ship's Condition and Damage (October 1823)**:
- **Orion** entered Toulon port after heavy weather for repairs
- Long ailing condition; barnacles on keel reduced speed; cleaned in dry dock year prior
- Cleaning damaged keel bolts; near Balearic Isles, sides strained, opened; ship sprung leak
- Violent equinoctial gale staved in grating and porthole on larboard side; damaged foretop-gallant-shrouds
- Forced return to Toulon for repairs; employed later at Brest as school-ship, Mediterranean squadron

**Topman's Fall and Rescue (October 1823, contemporary narrative)**:
- **Incident**: Crew busy bending sails; topman lost balance taking upper corner of main-topsail on starboard; fell, seized footrope with both hands, remained hanging at dizzy depth; shock imparted violent swinging motion; man swayed back and forth like stone in sling
- **Initial response**: No sailors (mostly fishermen recently levied) dared attempt rescue; topman losing strength, arms contracted in horrible twitchings; every ascent attempt increased oscillations; did not shout to conserve strength; all awaited moment of release
- **Convict rescuer**: Man in red (convict from galley detachment) dressed with green cap; had asked officer of watch permission to risk life saving topman; **broke chain riveted to ankle with one blow of hammer** (FACT: ease of chain-breaking noted only later, suspicious); caught rope, dashed into rigging
- **Rescue execution**: Convict climbed with tiger-cat agility; reached top, gust carried away cap revealing perfectly white head—not young man; measured yard with eye; fastened rope to yard point, allowed other end to hang; descended hand over hand; created second suspended figure over gulf instead of one
- **Crowd response**: Ten thousand glances fastened on group; not a cry, not a word; tremor contracted every brow; all held breath fearing slightest puff would add to wind swaying both men; anguish indescribable

**Metaphorical Significance**: Spider bringing life not death; moment of immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords men food for thought

## Ships of the Line: Structural and Philosophical Reflection
- Composed of heaviest/lightest matter; deals with solid, liquid, fluid; eleven iron claws seize granite seabed; wings/antennae catch wind; one hundred twenty cannons reply to thunder; ocean seeks to lead astray; compass shows north; lanterns supply stars; against wind: cordage/canvas; against water: wood; against rocks: iron/brass/lead; against shadows: light; against immensity: needle
- **Six-story construction stocks at Brest/Toulon**: Yard as colossal beam; main-mast sixty fathoms long, three feet diameter at base; English main-mast two hundred seventeen feet above water-line; three thousand cubic metres of wood required (floating forest); cables versus chains; chains pile four feet high, twenty feet broad, eight feet deep
- **Modern advancement (forty years post-narrative)**: Steam added new miracles; mixed vessel with screw propelled by three thousand square metres canvas and engine of two thousand five hundred horse-power
- **Vulnerability**: Gale breaks sixty-foot yard like straw; bends four-hundred-foot mast; twists anchor weighing tens of thousands in wave jaws like fisherman's hook; monstrous cannons utter plaintive futile roars; all power/majesty engulfed in superior power/majesty
- **Human curiosity**: Curious people abound in ports around these marvellous machines; daily from morning until night quays, sluices, jetties of Toulon port covered with idlers/loungers staring at **Orion**

## Main Characters Status (January 1823 onward)
- **Jean Valjean**: Imprisoned at Toulon (returned from M. sur M. arrest)
- **Fantine**: Dead, buried in pauper's grave
- **Cosette**: At Montfermeil with Thénardiers, awaiting rescue
- **Napoleon Bonaparte**: Defeated, imprisoned at Saint Helena, guarded by Hudson Lowe

## Themes
- Destiny/chance; divine intervention; human resilience amid opposing forces
- Waterloo as historical hinge; war's moral paradox; ceremony costs fortunes while poor starve
- Mundane life indifferent to empires/politics; daily tasks/debts/aches continue beneath grand narratives
- Mystery/obscurity: Boulatruelle's search; officer rescue; wagon woman; convict's suspicious chain-breaking ease; sealed letter to Dungate; Mill ledger rewritten; letters burned
- Hidden transgressions and buried truths
- Human courage in extremis: convict risking life; topman clinging to rope
- Immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought
